properties.name: Edge properties default like node properties do, and the sweep never looked at them
properties.statement:
The 2026-07-28 schema sweep behind req:defaults-do-not-assert measured NODE properties — ten of them across Requirement, Capability, Component, Constraint, DesignRule, Actor, EnvironmentRule and Flow. It never looked at EDGE properties, and the same defect is there. FOUND BY TRIPPING OVER IT: creating a DEPENDS_ON with no properties at all returned {"optional": false, "weight_basis": "estimated"} — materialised while capturing a requirement about exactly this.

MEASURED, not inspected, over the 3,226 edges of reflow2's own design. Nineteen edge properties carry a schema default. Four are single-valued wherever they appear, matching the default and never varying: ALLOCATED_TO.weight_basis = estimated on 96 of 96, DEPENDS_ON.optional = false on 123 of 123, PROVIDES.weight_basis and CONSUMES.weight_basis = estimated on 3 of 3 each.

THE SHARPEST FINDING IS WORSE THAN A DEFAULT THAT NEVER VARIES: it is a default that describes a value which does not exist. `weight_basis` is documented as "How the weight was set: an LLM estimate, grounded in evidence, or measured from telemetry." 225 edges carry weight_basis — ALLOCATED_TO 96, DEPENDS_ON 123, PROVIDES 3, CONSUMES 3 — and ZERO of them carry a `weight`. Every one of those edges states the provenance of a coupling strength that was never recorded. Note that variation does not rescue it: DEPENDS_ON.weight_basis genuinely varies (evidence on 70, estimated on 53), so it passes the single-valued test the node sweep used, and it is still describing nothing. The node sweep's own test — "a property that never varies is not carrying information" — is necessary but NOT sufficient on edges, because a property can vary and still refer to an absent value.

DEPENDS_ON.optional = false on 123 of 123 is a plain instance of the original rule: it asserts that every dependency in the design is MANDATORY, which is a real architectural claim and nobody made it.

LATENT, and it will assert on first use: ten defaulted edge properties sit on edge types with zero instances in this design — ANNOTATES.resolved, CAUSES.basis (`correlational`), CAUSES.validation_status, CLAIMS.depth, COMPLIES_WITH.verified, PART_OF_FLOW.weight_basis, SUPPLEMENTS.grounding (`extrapolated`), and VIOLATES_RULE.proposer / severity / status. VIOLATES_RULE.severity defaults to `high`, so the first rule violation anyone records will claim high severity unprompted. CAUSES.basis defaulting to `correlational` is the same shape one level up, and the edge's own hint says "Do not assert `causal` without a mechanism" — the schema warns against asserting the strong value while defaulting the weaker one.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT FROM THE PARENT APPLIES UNCHANGED: a default recording genuine ABSENCE is correct and must stay; only a default naming a CHOICE among alternatives lies. AUTHORED_BY.role (author 63 / approver 7 / reviewer 2) and CHANGED.accepted_baseline (true 232 / false 188) both vary and both carry information — they are not in scope. Also unchanged: altering a default is not retroactive, so edges already written keep what they were given and a sweep of existing designs is a separate deliberate act.

Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it. Not yet decided is whether `weight_basis` should default at all, or be absent until a weight exists — which is the same question ver:interface-spec answered for Interface.medium.
